chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding a male slave, so there happens to be for his master or for his mistress, a slave girl. So he intends to unite the two of them. Would he marry her to him with a valid marriage, or would it suffice him if he says, 'I have married you to so-and-so,' and he gives something from himself, or on behalf of the slave? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, and even if it is a mud (small measure), and I have seen him give a dirham.'

key_terms.الدِّرْهَمَ: The dirham (a coin used as dowry)

ai.seo_question: What is the procedure for a master to marry his male slave to his female slave?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that a master may marry his male slave to a female slave owned by the same master through either a formal contract or a simple declaration of marriage, provided a dowry is given. The Imam’s personal observation of giving even a single dirham underscores the Shia juristic principle that the dowry need not be substantial to validate the union, emphasizing accessibility and ease in manumission-related marriages. This ruling facilitates the social integration of slaves by allowing masters to marry them off without complex formalities, reflecting the pragmatic legal flexibility in al-Kafi.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban, from Muhammad Bin Muslim,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> regarding the owned slave, so there happens to be for his master or for her mistress, a slave girl. So he intends to gather between the two of them. Would his marriage be a (valid) marriage, or would it suffice him if he is saying, ‘I have married you to so and so woman, and he gives something from himself, or on behalf of the slave?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, and even if it is a handful, and it is my<sup>asws</sup> view that he should give the Dirham’.
